True coding regions that fail the coding test, and two fallbacks

This notebook supports the Results section “True coding regions that fail the coding test, and two fallbacks”, including its paragraph “Homology evidence recovers true coding regions, mostly in fragments” (../manuscript/sections/results_coding_failures.tex), and draws Fig. 5 (fig:failures, figures/fig5_failures.{pdf,png}). Provenance: E12 (the coding-failure analysis), E07 (homology runs of the benchmark) and E25 (final release runs).

Release rule. The analysis of E12 used the development rule: \(S_1>0\), frame contrast \(C=S_1-\max(S_2,S_3)>0\) and, below 300 nt, a fixed short-ORF test (\(C \ge 200\mu\)). The text still quotes it (it carries a \todo). Here the analysis is rerun on the release predictions (pytd_v7: PyTD 3a793ff, release defaults; Perl gives identical predictions, E25), with the release coding test: \(S_1>0\), \(C>0\) and target-decoy q-value \(\le 0.05\). The q-value of each candidate is read from the run’s decoy_qvalues.tsv.

Data (data/long_orf_failures/v7/, written by pipeline/derive/05_long_orf_failures_v7.sh, which runs 05_long_orf_failures_v7.py, 05_summarize_v7.py, 05_length_vs_homology_v7.py and 05_fig5_tables_v7.py; these are copies of analyses/long_orf_failures/*.py changed for the release rule):

  • the matched CDS tables of the 8 benchmark organisms (complete transcripts, UTRs trimmed to 250 nt), aggregated: by organism, length, GC3 quintile, chromosome, failure cause, and model;
  • homology flags from the release homology runs (pytd_v7_homology), which search all LongOrfs ORFs (\(\ge\) 50 aa) against Swiss-Prot (minus the organism’s own entries) and Pfam. E12 used older runs with a 100-aa minimum, so CDSs of 50–99 aa now have homology flags;
  • the truth-trained Markov models of E12 (two folds by gene) now pass an ORF only if it also has a q-value \(\le 0.05\) computed from decoys scored with the same model. The decoys are regenerated as PyTD generates them; with the run’s own model this reproduces every q-value in decoy_qvalues.tsv (checked below);
  • the homology comparison (Fig. 5d,e) uses data/benchmark/homology_v7h_vs_abinitio.tsv: the released homology mode (PyTD a5b24c3, homology-assisted start refinement; runs pytd_v7h_homology) minus the ab initio release runs (pytd_v7), from benchmark_v2/scripts/compare_homology.py on data/benchmark/final_v7/v7h_homology_scores.tsv (pipeline/derive/05_homology_v7h_table.sh; E25 addendum of 2026-10-28, E33). Selection and stops equal the earlier 3a793ff homology runs (pytd_v7_homology, homology_vs_abinitio.tsv, kept and compared below); only start codons differ. The development comparison (pytd_dev_v2_homology minus pytd_dev_v2) is kept as homology_vs_abinitio.dev_v2.tsv.
V7 <- function(f) read_tab("long_orf_failures", "v7", f)
by_org <- V7("summary_by_org.tsv")
by_len <- V7("summary_by_length.tsv")
oracle <- V7("oracle_models.tsv")
flags <- V7("explanation_flags.tsv")
rate_feat <- V7("fail_rate_by_feature.tsv")
by_chr <- V7("fail_by_chromosome.tsv") %>% mutate(seqid = as.character(seqid))
rp <- V7("ribosomal_proteins.tsv")
feat <- V7("features_fail_vs_pass.tsv")
fam <- V7("family_keyword_enrichment.tsv")
utr <- V7("utr_effect.tsv")
meta <- V7("org_meta.tsv")
lvh <- V7("length_vs_homology_fallback.tsv")
lro <- V7("length_rule_only_predictions.tsv") %>%
  separate(dataset, c("src", "org", "input"), sep = ":", remove = FALSE)
alt <- V7("alt_rules_negatives.tsv")
dmel_c <- V7("dmel_gc3_rescue.tsv")
long_fail <- V7("failing_ge1kb.tsv")
reasons <- V7("reasons_by_length.tsv")
hom <- read_tab("benchmark", "homology_v7h_vs_abinitio.tsv")
hom_3a7 <- read_tab("benchmark", "homology_vs_abinitio.tsv")  # 3a793ff homology runs (no start assist)
# development-rule tables of E12, for comparison
dev_by_org <- read_tab("long_orf_failures", "summary_by_org.tsv")
dev_by_len <- read_tab("long_orf_failures", "summary_by_length.tsv")

ALL <- by_org %>% filter(org == "ALL")
LEN_BINS <- c("0-299", "300-599", "600-999", "1000-1999", "2000-4999", ">=5000")

For every organism, the Markov scores recomputed here equal longest_orfs.cds.scores, and the q-values recomputed from the regenerated decoys equal decoy_qvalues.tsv for all 475,989 LongOrfs candidates. The same code therefore gives valid q-values for the truth-trained models below.

How often

fail_pct <- ALL$fail_coding_pct
len_all <- by_len %>% filter(org == "ALL") %>% mutate(cds_len_bin = factor(cds_len_bin, LEN_BINS)) %>% arrange(cds_len_bin)
lp <- setNames(len_all$fail_coding_pct, as.character(len_all$cds_len_bin))
reason_short <- len_all %>% filter(cds_len_bin == "0-299")
n_ge1kb <- nrow(long_fail)
named <- c("Muc14A", "kl-2", "kl-3", "MUC4", "FLG", "HRNR", "COL4A4", "ELN")
named_tab <- long_fail %>% filter(gene_name %in% named) %>%
  group_by(org, gene_name) %>% slice_max(cds_len, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
  select(org, gene_name, cds_len, fail_reason, category, decoy_q)
dev_all <- dev_by_org %>% filter(org == "ALL")

Of 135,429 annotated CDSs matched to a LongOrfs candidate (135,785 truth CDSs; E12 matched 135,429), 4.9% fail the release coding test (development rule: 4.9%). By cause: \(S_1 \le 0\) 3,091, shifted frame \(\ge S_1\) 1,189, q-value above 0.05 2,408. E12 E25

The failure rate by annotated CDS length (all organisms):

  left_join(dev_by_len %>% filter(org == "ALL") %>% select(cds_len_bin, dev_n = n, dev_fail_pct = fail_coding_pct),
            by = "cds_len_bin")

The length rule

tt_len <- by_len %>% filter(org == "tthermophila", cds_len_bin %in% c("1000-1999", "2000-4999", ">=5000"))
tt_lost_1kb <- sum(tt_len$still_lost)
# failing CDSs with an ORF at or above L* that the rule does not keep (should be T. thermophila only)
above_lstar <- by_len %>% filter(org != "ALL") %>% group_by(org) %>%
  summarise(rescued = sum(rescued_by_long_rule), still_lost = sum(still_lost), .groups = "drop")
lvh_all <- lvh %>% filter(org == "ALL")
lo_pct <- 100 * lvh_all$length_only / lvh_all$rescued_by_length
kable(lvh, caption = "Failing true CDSs retained by the length rule, and whether they also have a homology hit.")

The length rule keeps every failing CDS whose ORF reaches \(L^\ast\); it is off in T. thermophila, where 76 failing CDSs of at least 1 kb are lost. In total it retains 447 failing true CDSs; 85 (19.0%) of them have no Swiss-Prot or Pfam hit. E12

Why

Exclusive attribution (failures of at least 300 nt)

              unexplained = "unexplained")

Dropping \(S_1>0\) (keeping \(C>0\) and the q-value, recomputed with \(C>0\) as the only eligibility condition) adds -0.66–0.6% of true CDSs as candidates, while the number of random sequences with a candidate changes 1.4- to 7.9-fold (median 2.5). Candidate counts are upper bounds on calls (one ORF per transcript is kept). E12

Homology evidence recovers true coding regions, mostly in fragments

Release runs (pytd_v7 vs pytd_v7h_homology, PyTD a5b24c3 with the homology-assisted start refinement; data/benchmark/homology_v7h_vs_abinitio.tsv). E25 E33

  • Complete transcripts (48 inputs): stop-level sensitivity -0.3 to +3.7 points; exact F1 -0.4 to +4.8 points.
  • Fragments (32 inputs): sensitivity +0.4 to +9.2; exact F1 +0.5 to +12.9 points.
  • Stranded fragments, exact F1: human +11.8, mouse +10.9, A. thaliana +9.4; the other five organisms +0.5 to +6.5 points.
  • Stop-level precision, all inputs without lncRNAs: -0.5 to +1.3 points. Calls on random sequences rose by 0–2 per input in seven organisms and 12–39 in T. thermophila.
  • Human lncRNAs with a prediction: 1,639 to 3,268 (mouse 1,640 to 2,452). Exact F1 with lncRNA negatives: complete human +0.6, mouse +1.4; fragments human +8.8, mouse +9.6 points.

        legend.text = element_text(size = 5), legend.key.size = unit(2.2, "mm"))
pC <- ggplot(pc, aes(x)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = fail_pct, fill = "fail"), width = 0.72) +
  geom_col(aes(y = rescued_pct, fill = "rescued by GC3-matched model"), width = 0.72) +
  geom_text(aes(y = fail_pct + 1, label = label), vjust = 0, size = 1.8, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 4.8, colour = "#bbbbbb", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted") +

        legend.position.inside = c(0.5, 0.82), legend.text = element_text(size = 5.5))
hom_panel <- function(col, ylab) {
  ggplot(pde, aes(org, .data[[col]], fill = variant)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.55), width = 0.5) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(complete = COMPLETE_C, fragments = FRAG_C), name = NULL) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.5, max(10, ceiling(max(pde$sens, pde$f1x))))) + labs(x = NULL, y = ylab) + ital_x
}
pD <- hom_panel("sens", "homology − ab initio:\nstop-level sensitivity (points)") + theme(legend.position = "top")
pE <- hom_panel("f1x", "homology − ab initio:\nexact-CDS F1 (points)") + theme(legend.position = "none")

  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`also a homology hit` = "#9ecae1", `length rule only` = TD_C), name = NULL) +

  theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.7, 0.2), axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
fig5 <- (pA | pB | pC) / (pD | pE | pF) + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.85)) +
